title: Why 'Sitting Straight' Gets Tiring
body: Holding any single posture — even a textbook upright one — fatigues muscles after 30 minutes. Shifting between reclined support, upright sitting, and brief standing keeps spinal discs nourished.

title: Skip Neck Circles, Try the Chin Nod
body: Full head circles can compress sensitive cervical joints. Instead, glide your chin gently straight back 1 cm while keeping your gaze level — it lengthens the back of the neck safely.

title: The 20-20-20 Eye & Neck Connection
body: When your eyes lock onto a close screen, your suboccipital neck muscles automatically tense to stabilize your gaze. Looking 20 feet away for 20 seconds relaxes both your eyes and upper neck.

title: 2 Minutes Every Hour Beats 1 Long Sit
body: Short 2-minute standing or walking breaks activate your calf muscle pump, boosting blood flow and clearing afternoon brain fog without breaking a sweat.

title: Float Your Wrists While Typing
body: Resting the crease of your wrist hard against the desk edge compresses tendons. Let your forearms take the support and keep your wrists straight and relaxed.
